title: LQ Sentinel Orchestrator for KV-pack & Batch-shape Config Changes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight 'LQ Sentinel' orchestrator that runs targeted latency-vs-quality checks whenever batching/kv-cache config or model variant changes are proposed. The goal is to automate early detection of quality regressions that are subtle (small but user-visible) and correlate them with config deltas, while simultaneously surfacing latency tail regressions so rollouts can make informed trade-offs. This ticket covers design, eval harness integration, alert thresholds, and a canary gating job that runs as part of the CI/rollout pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible CI job (lq-sentinel) is created and runs automatically for PRs that touch batching/kvcache or model-selection files.
The job emits a bounded report (JSON + HTML) that contains: per-slice quality delta, model-similarity embeddings, and latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for the changed config vs baseline.

Regression / improvement signals use agreed heuristics: >=1.0% drop in synthetic-accuracy or >=0.8% drop in embed-similarity triggers a WARNING; >=2.5% drop triggers a FAIL gate. p95 latency increase >20% triggers a WARN; >40% triggers FAIL.
Dashboard panel and Slack alert channel (runtime-lq-alerts) receive summarized findings with links to the full report and failing examples.
Playbook created for reviewers that maps typical failure modes to remediation actions (tune microbatch, increase KV TTL, fallback to model variant).
Integration tests that validate the sentinel runs end-to-end on a mock workload (sanity run takes < 12 minutes).
Documentation page with example outputs and instructions for adding new slices is published in Confluence.
Rolling canary gate in the console uses the sentinel report to block rollouts when a FAIL is produced.

eval_design_notes: Slices include: short prompts (<30 tokens), long prompts (>512 tokens), multi-turn chats with cache reuse, high-entropy code-completion samples.
Quality metrics: embed-sim (cosine of instruction-tuned embed model), answer-accuracy (task-specific correctness), hallucination-score (NLI-based detector), and BLEU/ROUGE for structured tasks.
Baseline: use the current default runtime config pinned in runtime-configs/prod/baseline.json. The sentinel compares candidate config against the last green baseline commit.
Sampling regime: deterministic seeded sample of 5k examples out of the canonical eval corpus stratified by customer slice and token-length distribution.
Latency measurement: real end-to-end through the same RPC path used in production with KV cache warmup phases and cold-cache windows to measure both steady-state and miss-path latency.
Statistical test: bootstrap difference-in-means with 95% CI; flag only when effect size exceeds both practical significance and statistical significance to avoid noisy alerts.
Artifacts include example failing pairs (prompt + candidate output + baseline output) to aid triage.
We will store reports in s3://redwood-lq-sentinel/reports/{key}/{timestamp}.html and expose them through the console for reviewers.
tradeoffs: Run-time vs coverage: larger sample sets increase signal fidelity but add CI latency. Chosen compromise: stratified 5k sample with fast embed-sim checks and a smaller (500) human-like QA bucket for higher-cost detectors.
Strict gates reduce regressions in production but will slow feature rollouts; initial phase uses WARN-only for non-P0 until team is comfortable, then escalate to FAIL for P0 changes.
KV-cache TTL tuning can mask quality regressions (by changing cached prefixes). Sentinel will surface both immediate quality deltas and temporal drift signals to catch such masking.
Latency measurement instrumentation increases trace noise and storage; we limit detailed traces to failing runs and summary metrics otherwise.
False positives from synthetic corpora: to mitigate, we will maintain a customer-representative slice and allow teams to annotate ignored regressions in the report.
